content.user_title: Draft US Grant Proposals and Budget Narratives
content.value_statement: US grant applications require coordinated narratives, budgets, and compliance checks. This guide helps structure working drafts and identify requirements for human review.
actual_capabilities: Guides prospect research and fit assessment using Grants.gov, foundation filings, and state portals.
Structures proposal sections covering needs, objectives, methods, evaluation, sustainability, and organizational capacity.
Guides line-item budgets and matching narratives, including discussion of the 15% de minimis indirect rate.
Organizes compliance reviews for announcement requirements, page limits, attachments, and registration prerequisites.
Guides SBIR/STTR Phase I proposal skeletons for NSF, NIH, and DoD.
Links proposed activities to outcomes and budget lines through a logic-model-first approach.
limitations: Covers US grants only and does not submit applications.
Produces working drafts that require human review and current funder guidance.
Includes no bundled scripts, extension source, or template files; live research depends on the host agent and available tools.
Indirect rate eligibility, MTDC exclusions, and agency requirements must be verified for each award.

use_cases.title: Prepare a first federal proposal
use_cases.description: Organize program information into narrative sections, a preliminary budget, and a compliance checklist.

use_cases.title: Revise a rejected application
use_cases.description: Compare reviewer feedback with evaluation criteria and identify changes to objectives, methods, and budget alignment.

use_cases.title: Outline a Phase I application
use_cases.description: Develop an agency-focused SBIR/STTR proposal skeleton and identify registration requirements to verify.

prompt_templates.title: Outline a first proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a proposal outline for [program] using [funder announcement]. Include required narrative sections and mark missing organizational information.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a budget justification
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a budget narrative from [line-item budget] and [award guidance]. Identify missing figures and explain which indirect cost assumptions need verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: connecting costs to program activities.

prompt_templates.title: Review narrative consistency
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [proposal draft] against [review criteria]. Build a logic model linking activities, measurable outcomes, and budget lines. Flag gaps without inventing evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: aligning evaluation, narrative, and costs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Phase I draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [SBIR/STTR Phase I draft] against [agency announcement]. List narrative gaps, page limits, required attachments, and registration prerequisites. Separate verified requirements from unresolved questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: preparing a proposal for final human review.

output_examples.input: Outline a federal grant proposal for a nonprofit workforce training program. The funder announcement has not been provided.
output: Need statement: Add local employment data and evidence of training barriers.
Objectives: Define participant numbers, completion targets, and employment outcomes.
Methods: Describe recruitment, training delivery, and employer partnerships.
Evaluation: Specify measures, data sources, and reporting intervals.
Compliance: Confirm required sections and page limits after receiving the announcement.

output_examples.input: Draft budget justification headings for a $250,000 federal request using a proposed 15% de minimis indirect rate.
output: Personnel: Provide roles, effort, salary assumptions, and links to proposed activities.
Fringe benefits: Provide the applicable rate and calculation basis.
Other direct costs: Itemize program expenses and explain their purpose.
Indirect costs: Confirm eligibility and the MTDC base before applying the proposed 15% rate.
Missing information: Supply cost figures and award guidance before calculating totals.

best_practices: Provide the current funder announcement, review criteria, and any reviewer feedback before drafting.
Use verified organizational facts and budget figures; mark missing evidence instead of filling gaps with assumptions.
Recheck calculations, indirect cost eligibility, attachments, and portal requirements before a human submits the application.
anti_patterns: Treating a generated draft as submission-ready or assuming the skill files applications.
Applying a 15% indirect rate without checking eligibility, award terms, and the correct MTDC base.
Inventing impact statistics, partnerships, registrations, or financial information to complete a proposal.

faq.question: Does this skill submit grant applications?
faq.answer: No. It guides drafting and compliance review, but a person must verify and submit the application.

faq.question: Does it cover grants outside the United States?
faq.answer: No. The guide focuses on US federal, foundation, and state grant workflows.

faq.question: Which proposal sections can it help organize?
faq.answer: It covers need statements, objectives, methods, evaluation, sustainability, organizational capacity, and budget narratives.

faq.question: Does it support SBIR and STTR proposals?
faq.answer: The guide describes Phase I skeletons for NSF, NIH, and DoD. Verify eligibility and current agency instructions separately.

faq.question: Is the 15% indirect rate always applicable?
faq.answer: No. The guide discusses the 15% de minimis rate, but eligibility, award terms, and MTDC exclusions require verification.

faq.question: Are research tools or templates included?
faq.answer: No. This folder contains only the guide. Live research requires tools available through your host agent, and original package templates are absent.
